author: Marcus R. Brown
description:
Tab completion split the command line on whitespace, so a quoted argument containing a space was torn into separate tokens. Completing `cat "my doc<TAB>` saw `['cat', '"my', 'doc']` and matched candidates against `doc` instead of `my doc`.

```ts
// Parse command parts using simple whitespace splitting for now
// TODO: Enhance with proper shell parsing that handles quotes, escaping, etc.
const commandParts = inputToCursor.trim().split(/\s+/).filter(part => part.length > 0)
```

## The second instance

Fixing the tokenizer alone would not have been enough. `applySuggestion` independently re-derived the word boundary when a provider does not set an explicit `suggestion.range` — which is every provider today:

```ts
const words = beforeCursor.split(/\s+/)
const currentWord = words.at(-1) ?? ''
const wordStart = beforeCursor.lastIndexOf(currentWord)
```

Two problems. It repeats the same whitespace assumption, and `lastIndexOf` searches the entire prefix rather than locating the current token — so a repeated word matches the wrong occurrence. Accepting a completion on `cat "my doc` produced `cat "my my doc.txt`: quote stranded, wrong span replaced.

This is the path that actually corrupts the user's input, and it needed the span data, which is why the offset has to travel through `CompletionContext` rather than staying local to `createCompletionContext`.

## Approach

`parser.ts` already had a quote-aware state machine that tolerates unterminated quotes — `parseCommand('echo "unclosed')` returns `['echo', 'unclosed']` rather than throwing, which matters because mid-typing input almost always has an open quote. What it lacked was raw position: `parseCommand` returns stripped strings, and a stripped token cannot tell you where its opening quote was. [description truncated to fit budget]
title: fix(moo-dang): use real shell tokenizer for tab completion
